segments.text: Big idea! Nebuchadnezzar's forgotten dream is God's roadmap for history. It shows that all human
rule is limited, that it passes away, and that it will be replaced by the everlasting kingdom of
Jesus Christ. From the Last Sitting. Sitting 1. In chapter 1, Daniel and his companions show that
loyalty at the table preceded the gift of wisdom. Daniel 1.8, Daniel 1.17. Now, in chapter 2, that
wisdom is tested on the global stage, when the emperor dreams of the fate of all human empires,
and heaven, not Babylon's magicians, defines what shall be in the latter days.
Introduction. The impasse of human wisdom. Daniel 2.1-28. Babylon. The second year,
counted from 605 BC, the year Nebuchadnezzar became king. In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar's
reign, Daniel 2.1, about 603 BC, counting from 605 BC, the year he became king, the king of
Babylon was awakened by a terrifying nightmare that left his spirit deeply agitated. Seeking certainty,
the king summoned his occult counselors, the magicians and the astrologers and the sorcerers
and the Chaldeans, and placed before them an impossible demand. The king had forgotten his
dream. The thing is gone from me. And they had to tell him both the dream and its meaning,
or face immediate execution. Daniel 2.2-5. Babylon's wise men admitted they had no answer.
There is not a man upon the earth that can show the king's matter, except the gods, whose
dwelling is not with flesh. Daniel 2.10-11. KJV. When the royal execution decree went forth,
Daniel and his companions did not panic. They held an emergency prayer session,
petitioning the god of heaven for mercy concerning this secret. Daniel 2.17-18.
In a night vision, God revealed both the dream and its meaning.
Standing before the emperor, Daniel deflected all praise from human intellect to divine sovereignty.
There is a god in heaven that revealeth secrets, and maketh known to the king Nebuchadnezzar
what shall be in the latter days. Daniel 2.28. KJV.
The forgotten dream was not an ancient puzzle designed to satisfy curiosity.
This sitting reads it as God's roadmap for history, which says that all human rule is limited
and passes away, and that it will be replaced by the everlasting kingdom of Jesus Christ.
The statue and the stone described below are the reasons for that claim.
Text. Human wisdom failed. Daniel prayed. God revealed secrets. The dream governs the latter
days. The king's magicians do not. Main point one. The historicist chain of world empires.
Daniel 2.31-40. Nebuchadnezzar saw an immense, dazzling statue standing before him.
Daniel 2.31. Its body had five parts. A head of fine gold, his breast and his arms of silver,
his belly and his thighs of brass, his legs of iron, and his feet part of iron and part of clay.
Daniel 2.32-33. This sequence presents an unbroken, continuous chain of empires in historical time.
Reading prophecy this way, as one unbroken history, is called the historicist reading,
which sitting zero introduced. Head of gold. Babylon. 605-539 BC,
counted from the year Nebuchadnezzar became king. Daniel identifies the starting point without
ambiguity. Thou art this head of gold. Daniel 2.38. Scripture calls Babylon the golden city,
Isaiah 14.4, which had its golden age in the days of King Nebuchadnezzar, 605-562 BC.
The king confessed God when he heard the dream. He fell on his face and said,
of a truth it is, that your God is a God of gods and a Lord of kings. Daniel 2.46-47.
That confession did not stop the dream. The same chapter still names the kingdom that follows his
own and the kingdom that replaces them all. Chest and arms of silver. Medo-Persia, 539-331 BC.
Daniel announces that after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee. Daniel 2.39.
Daniel 2 does not name that second kingdom. It only says another kingdom comes after Babylon.
This reading calls it Medo-Persia because Belshazzar, Babylon's last king, is slain and a median,
a man from Media, the land beside Persia, takes the kingdom. Daniel 5.30-31. And Daniel 8.20
names the ram as the kings of Media and Persia. Cyrus, the Persian king named in Daniel 1.21,
6.28, and 10.1, belongs to that same power. Succession remains the after thee of Daniel 2.39.
Belly and thighs of bronze. Greece, 3.31-168 BC. A third kingdom of brass which shall bear rule
over all the earth followed. Daniel 2.39. The Persian empire was defeated by Alexander at Arbela
or Gaugamela, 3.31 BC. Daniel 8.21 names the rough goat as the king of Grisha. Daniel 8.7
says the goat smote the ram and break his two horns. And Daniel 8.20 names that ram as the kings
of Media and Persia. Legs of iron. Imperial Rome, 168 BC to AD 476. The fourth kingdom shall be
strong as iron, for as much as iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things. Daniel 2.40.
Daniel 2 does not print the name Rome. It says the fourth kingdom is strong as iron and breaks
the kingdoms before it and it comes after Greece. This reading names that kingdom Rome.
It runs from the Battle of Pidna in 168 BC where Rome ended the Macedonian monarchy to AD 476.
In that year a Germanic general removed the last emperor in the west and the one kingdom broke
into the separate kingdoms that became the feet. Two trends inside the colossus. Value falls,
force rises. The colossus shows two opposite trends at once. Value declines, iron is stronger.
Daniel 2.39 says the next kingdom is inferior. 2.40 says the fourth is strong as iron.
Hardness and crushing force increase. While gold and silver are malleable and soft, iron possesses
brutal crushing force. Imperial Rome possessed military destructiveness. In plain words,
God showed Nebuchadnezzar one line of four kingdoms and then a kingdom he sets up himself
that never ends. Interpretation. Daniel 2 is the chapter the whole course rests on,
so it is worth saying exactly what it does and does not name. It names one kingdom and one king.
Everything else in the chain has to be read from the order the chapter gives
and from the later visions that name the same powers. Here is what is named.
Daniel 2.38 says to Nebuchadnezzar, thou art this head of gold. That is the first kingdom.
Babylon. Daniel 2.39 then says, after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee
and another third kingdom of brass. Daniel 2.40 says the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron.
So the statue gives an order of four kingdoms and never pauses between them.
Here is where the names come from. The second and third are named in a later vision.
Daniel 8.20 calls the ram the kings of Media and Persia and Daniel 8.21 calls the goat the king
of Grisha. That makes Greece the bronze of Daniel 2 and Media and Persia the silver.
The fourth kingdom, the iron, is Rome and this course reads it from history.
The power that followed Greece over the same lands broke them and ruled them.
Two rules follow and they are the reason the chain holds together.
First, you start at the head that is named and walk forward.
You do not restart the chain in a later century. Second, the feet are the same fourth kingdom,
divided, not a fifth empire that appears after a long wait. Daniel 2.41 says of the feet,
the kingdom shall be divided, but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron.
Iron is still in the mixture. The fourth kingdom is still what the feet are made of.
Then the stone strikes in the days of these kings and the kingdom it sets up shall never be destroyed.
Daniel 2.44. The bottom line is that the dream is not a chart of four interesting empires.
It is a single line drawn by God and it ends in a kingdom he gives rather than one a king builds.
We have come to the first checkpoint. Main point two, the divided kingdoms and
the mirage of unity. Daniel 2.41-43. The statue does not feature a fifth metal.
In this image, each new metal marks a new empire. So, where no new metal comes,
no new world empire comes either. The legs of iron transition directly into
feet composed of iron mixed with miry clay. Daniel 2.41-43. And iron and clay do not fuse into one.
Daniel himself says what this mixture means. The kingdom shall be divided. Daniel 2.41.
It is the same kingdom, divided, and no longer a single world empire. In A.D. 476 it divided
into separate kingdoms, the successor nations, as the Roman West fell to Germanic peoples such
as the Goths, the Franks, and the Lombards. Iron and clay. What Daniel 2.41-43 says
and how this sitting reads it. Daniel 2.41. The kingdom shall be divided,
but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron, forasmuch as thou sawest the iron mixed with
miry clay. Daniel 2.42. So the kingdom shall be partly strong and partly broken. Daniel 2.43.
They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men, but they shall not cleave one to another,
even as iron is not mixed with clay. No fifth metal appears. The feet are part iron
and part potter's clay. Daniel 2.41. Read historically, the feet are divided Europe
after Rome. Verse 41 says the divided kingdom still has the strength of the iron in it,
so the iron is Rome's hardness still alive in the kingdoms that grew out of it.
The clay stands for the peoples of divided Western Europe, mixed in as the empire broke up. The feet
stand in the lands the iron legs ruled, and the chapter calls this half of the kingdom
partly broken, while the iron half stays strong. Daniel 2.42. Verse 43 says they shall mingle
themselves with the seed of men, and seed of men means human offspring, so the mingling points
to marriages. This reading takes it as royal intermarriage between ruling houses made to join
kingdoms together and it does not hold. Daniel 2.43. Daniel 11 uses the same motif. A royal
marriage made to seal an agreement does not stand. Daniel 11.6.17. Some historicists take
the clay as religious power allied with the state. That reading has to lean on Revelation 17,
where a woman rides a beast with ten horns. 17.3, 12-13, 16-17. Revelation 18.4 then calls God's
people out of her. A reader holds that view by carrying the picture back into Daniel's clay.
The woman is the religious power, the beast is the state that carries her,
and the mixture of iron and clay is read as their union in the last days.
This sitting does not build on that, because Daniel 2 itself explains the feet in political terms.
The kingdom shall be divided, 241, the seed of men, 243, and these kings, 244.
Some rulers have tried to unite Europe again. Charles the Great, Charlemagne, around AD 800,
Charles V in 1519, Napoleon from 1804 to 1815, and Hitler from 1939 to 1945.
Verse 43 names no ruler and no date. It says that the iron and the clay will mix and still not join,
and this reading takes those later attempts as fitting that picture,
because each one tried to hold many peoples under a single rule and each broke apart.
The mixture does not hold. They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men,
but they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay. Daniel 243, KJV.
We have come to the second checkpoint, main point three, the redemptive climax,
the supernatural stone. The focal point of the vision is not the metallic colossus,
but its total destruction by a supernatural agent. Thou sawest till that a stone was cut
out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay
and break them to pieces. And the stone that smote the image became a great mountain
and filled the whole earth. Daniel 234 to 35, KJV.
One, the divine identity of the stone. The stone is Jesus Christ. Cut out without hands
means the kingdom is of God, not of human empire building. Daniel 234, 44 to 45.
The strike falls on the feet in the days of these kings, the divided era after Rome,
so the climax is the second coming, not the incarnation.
Jesus' earthy ministry took place during the iron legs. The stone does not strike the legs.
The verses below call Jesus a stone or a rock, but that does not by itself prove that Daniel's
stone is him. The timing and the kind of kingdom do. Jesus came during the iron legs,
and Daniel's stone strikes later, at the feet, so the strike is his return at the end.
And Daniel's stone is cut out without hands, set up by the God of heaven,
and becomes a kingdom that shall stand forever. Daniel 244. Only Christ's kingdom fits that.
Scripture also calls Jesus the stone, the stone rejected by the builders that becomes
the chief cornerstone, Psalm 118.22, 1 Peter 2.6-8. The rock that followed them,
and that rock was Christ, 1 Corinthians 10.4. The rock upon which the church is built,
Matthew 16.18. The stone that shatters all opposition, Luke 20.17-18.
2. The timing and nature of the impact. The location of the strike. The stone strikes the
statue on its feet of iron and clay, Daniel 234. It did not strike during the Babylonian,
Persian, Greek, or unified pagan Roman legs. Verse 44 establishes the timeline,
and in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom which shall never be
destroyed. So the kingdom arrives in the divided era, not before it. That era is the feet,
and this reading dates its start to AD 476. The kingdom does not arrive until the divided nations
are on the scene. Abolition, not political reformation. The stone does not merge with
the statue, reform its politics, or Christianize its laws through social evolution. It strikes
the image with overwhelming force and crushes all human empires to powder so that they blow
away like the dry husks left on a threshing floor carried off by the wind. Daniel 235.
A universal, eternal domain. After breaking the Colossus to pieces,
the stone grows into a great mountain that fills the whole earth. Revelation 11.15 says the
kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord and of his Christ,
and he shall reign forever and ever. 3. The redemptive choice. Repentance or ruin.
Jesus spoke of the stone in words that echo Daniel 2, where the stone ground the statue to chaff,
Daniel 2.35. Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken, but on whosoever it shall fall,
it will grind him to powder. Luke 2018. KJV. Luke 2018 echoes the stone image.
The words that carry the echo are that stone and grind him to powder. The same stone Daniel
saw and the same crushing that turned the statue to chaff. Daniel 2.35. Luke never names Daniel,
so this sitting reads the line as an allusion, not as a quotation of the prophet.
If you fall upon Christ today in contrite repentance, your sins are forgiven through
his blood, and you are saved. Ephesians 1.7. On whosoever it shall fall, it will grind him
to powder. Luke 2018. Christ. The stone is not a policy program or a better emperor.
It is Jesus Christ, cut without hands, striking the feet, filling the earth.
Build on the living stone today. We have come to the third checkpoint.
4. Why historicism protects Christian hope. Historicism, the reading this course follows,
takes Daniel 2 as one unbroken history from Babylon to the end of time. It keeps Daniel 2's named head
and unbroken after the succession. The chain remains unbroken. Daniel 2.38 establishes Babylon
as the historical head. Each subsequent medal follows consecutively. After thee shall arise
the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron. Daniel 2.40. Historicism respects this language
by tracing history continuously from 605 BC, the year Nebuchadnezzar became king,
through divided Europe to the end of time. Preterism and futurism break the text.
Two other readings break this one story, and the chapter itself shows why neither fits.
Sitting zero gives each one a full card. Here is what each claims and why people hold it.
Preterism ends the dream too soon. Preterism says the dream was fulfilled in the past,
soon after it was given. Its best known form is the Maccabean reading. The prophecy ends in the
second century BC when Antiochus IV Epiphanes, the Greek Syrian king, attacked the Jews and
defiled their temple, and the Maccabees, the Jewish family who led the revolt, fought back.
An ancient critic named Porphyry argued for that reading.
People hold it because it ties the dream to events anyone can look up in history,
and because it lets the book speak to the people who first read it.
But the chapter does not stop there. After the bronze, it still describes the legs of iron,
Rome, the divided feet, and the stone that fills the earth, Daniel 2.33-35. If the dream
ended with Antiochus, those parts would have nowhere to go. One form of this reading
takes the divided feet for the provinces the Greek kings fought over after Alexander died,
the lands ruled by the line of Greek kings called Seleucid, and the stone for the Jewish state the
Maccabees set up in the hundreds BC. That does not fit either. In this chapter,
the divided feet come after the iron, the fourth kingdom, while those provinces are pieces of
Greece, the third. And the kingdom the stone sets up fills the whole earth and stands forever,
Daniel 2.44, whereas the Jewish state that came out of the revolt ended under Rome.
Futurism cuts the dream in the middle. Futurism says the last part of the prophecy is still ahead
of us. It lets the statue run as far as Rome, then inserts a gap of about 2,000 years before
the feet. During that pause, the prophetic clock stops, and the final events are kept
for a short crisis just before Christ returns. People hold it because they expect that crisis
before Christ comes, and the Bible does speak of one, Daniel 12.1. But Daniel 2.41 says the feet are
the same fourth kingdom, divided. The kingdom shall be divided, but there shall be in it of
the strength of the iron. A kingdom that goes on, divided, is not a new one that starts after
a long wait. The passage prints no gap, so the gap has to be brought in from outside.
Only the historicist reading takes the statue as the chapter gives it. Head to feet, then the
stone, with nothing missing and nothing added. Continuity matters for a reason you can check in
the chapter itself. It gives an order, one kingdom after another, then a third, then a fourth,
and it never pauses. Add a gap from outside the passage, and the centuries we live in have no place
left on the line. You know your place on the timeline. On this reading, the feet run from AD
476 until the stone strikes. More than 15 centuries of that stretch have already passed,
and the feet are the last stage of the image, so we live in the toes, near its end. The chapter
gives no date for the strike, so this reading cannot say how near the end is. What it can say
is that no part of the image comes after the feet. The next major event on heaven's prophetic
calendar is not another world empire, but the return of Jesus Christ to set up his eternal
kingdom. Before you accept a prophetic conclusion text, does Daniel 2.38 fix Babylon as the
non-repeatable head? History. Does the chain stay contiguous from gold to iron and clay feet?
Interpretation. Does the stone strike the feet in the days of these kings, not through human
evolution? Christ. Does this lead you to the stone who fills the earth, or to fear of a
restarting head of gold? Christology. The supernatural stone and the sovereign triumph
of Christ. The stone cut out without hands is Jesus Christ, a kingdom of divine origin,
not human agency. The strike is at the feet in the days of these kings, the second coming,
not the incarnation. Daniel 2.34, 44-45. He is the chief cornerstone the builders rejected.
Psalm 118.22, Luke 2017. The rock upon which the church is built. Matthew 16.18.
And the stone that grinds to powder the one on whom it falls. Luke 2018. The stone strikes the
feet in the days of these kings, during divided Europe. It pulverizes every metal kingdom at once
and becomes a mountain filling the whole earth. Christ does not reform empires. He abolishes them
and establishes an everlasting kingdom. Daniel 2.44-45. Rev. 11.15. Whosoever shall fall upon
that stone shall be broken. But on whosoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.
Luke 2018. Build your hope on the living stone, not on the crumbling feet of iron and clay.
